texts.label: text
texts.orig: Watts Cemetery Chapel is free to explore as part of your visit. It's a short walk from our Visitor Centre, on Down Lane.
texts.text: Watts Cemetery Chapel is free to explore as part of your visit. It's a short walk from our Visitor Centre, on Down Lane.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: This unique Grade I-listed terracotta building is the work of artist and designer Mary Watts. Over 70 people from the local community helped her create it between 1895 and 1904. It opened in 1898 and remains a working chapel to this day.
texts.text: This unique Grade I-listed terracotta building is the work of artist and designer Mary Watts. Over 70 people from the local community helped her create it between 1895 and 1904. It opened in 1898 and remains a working chapel to this day.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Clay tiles decorate the outside. They blend Celtic, Romanesque, and Art Nouveau influences. Inside the Chapel you will find one of the most important and experimental wall paintings in England.
texts.text: Clay tiles decorate the outside. They blend Celtic, Romanesque, and Art Nouveau influences. Inside the Chapel you will find one of the most important and experimental wall paintings in England.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The cemetery is more than 120 years old. It was laid out by Mary Watts between 1895 and 1898, with the help of Compton Parish Council.
texts.text: The cemetery is more than 120 years old. It was laid out by Mary Watts between 1895 and 1898, with the help of Compton Parish Council.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: 'This miracle in terracotta stretches across the exterior of the building, where ancient symbols of hope, liberty and spirituality adorn buttresses, capitals and columns.'
